newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Explosions hit Bosnian village near communal line.
newsitem.headline: Explosions hit Bosnian village near communal line.

text.p: Two explosions have damaged homes being built by Bosnian Moslems trying to resettle their village near the country's communal boundary line, international police monitors reported on Friday.

The blasts occurred within five minutes of one another, shortly before 8 p.m. on Thursday in Gajevi village in northeastern Bosnia, said Andrea Angelli, spokesman for the International Police Task Force.
"An explosion has destroyed one of these prefabricated houses in Gajevi, three other houses suffered minor damge," Angelli told Reuters.
A Russian soldier in the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) was slightly injured by debris, he said.
Tensions have been running high around the village after a group of Moslem refugees tried to move back to pre-war homes now in Serb-controlled territory.

Serb mobs have attacked Moslem builders putting up temporary housing for 36 families who plan to resettle Gajevi. The families previously submitted to a vetting procedure supervised by international agencies.
SFOR has stepped up U.S.-Russian patrols in the area to try to defuse tensions but says it is up to Serb police to ensure the safety of the Moslem refugees.
American and Russian soldiers, however, spotted Serb police planting a booby-trap on the road to Gajevi last month.
About 40 construction workers travel to Gajevi every day under escort by SFOR and leave before nightfall.
A firefight broke out in November when Moslem refugees tried to enter Gajevi. A Serb man died and two Moslems were wounded in the violence.
On Thursday, two explosions rocked the divided Bosnian city of Mostar as tensions ran high again between the rival Croat and Moslem communities, U.N. officials reported.
